objectives.text: Review RFC 0011 v1.3 line by line for normative language and requirement quality: RFC 2119 as clarified by RFC 8174 (keywords in uppercase only where normative; a lowercase must, should or may in a normative clause is ambiguous); every MUST and MUST NOT names its actor and can be verified by a test or an inspection; every SHOULD says or implies when departing from it is acceptable; every requirement is singular (one obligation), unambiguous and free of vague terms (for example short, large, well within); passive voice that hides who acts; and the requirement characteristics of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 (necessary, unambiguous, complete, singular, feasible, verifiable, correct, consistent). Report each defect with the RFC line and the exact replacement text.

constraints.text: Read-only: do not edit, commit or push any repository file, and do not comment on or edit any issue or PR. Write only in your scratch directory and your AAR file.
Do not alter a quotation of the commander: quoted text keeps its spelling, spacing and punctuation. Propose changes to the RFC's own prose only.
Do not reopen the commander's decisions (D874d-<n>); a decision you judge unsound is a proposal, not a defect.
Cite every defect by its RFC line number, as read from disk when you start, and quote the text. Every proposal gives the exact old text and new text.

When you cite a standard's wording (RFC 2119, RFC 8174, RFC 7322, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148), read it in the browser through the chrome-devtools skill; if the browser is unavailable, use WebFetch and say so. Say unknown rather than quote from memory.
Stop every background shell and monitor you start before you hand back.
